profile: I'm a 60-year-old woman. My first language is English. I'm vegan: no meat, fish, dairy, eggs or honey. A vegan filter would matter to me because I check labels every time I shop. I have never bought groceries online. I use websites and apps every day, but I don't explore features unless I need them. I'm reasonably patient, but I don't like wasting time. I know the hidden animal ingredients, like whey, casein, gelatin, albumin, carmine and lard. I read the start of an ingredient list, not every word, and sometimes I miss things. I'm doing this on my phone.

I'm a 37-year-old man. My first language is Chinese (Mandarin). I eat meat and dairy and don't think much about it. Honestly, I'm skeptical about vegan products and don't see why a supermarket needs special features for them. I buy groceries online a few times a month. I'm not very comfortable with websites and apps. I read slowly, I don't always know what icons mean, and I usually don't notice small buttons or menus. I'm patient and careful. I'd rather read the details than make a mistake. I only know the obvious things: meat, fish, milk and eggs. Words like whey, casein, gelatin or albumin don't mean anything to me, and I'm not sure whether honey counts. I usually go by a product's name and picture, and at most glance at the first few ingredients. I often miss small print and sometimes tap the wrong thing. I'm doing this on my phone.
